FoxG1 (Forkhead box protein G1) is a winged-helix DNA-binding transcription factor / transcriptional repressor with a forkhead binding domain that represses target genes during brain development; key role in early telencephalon patterning

Recruits transcriptional co-repressors via two protein-binding domains: JARID1B-binding domain (JBD, recruits JARID1C demethylase involved in H3K4 demethylation) and Groucho-binding domain (GBD, interacts with Groucho); FoxG1 also interacts with the androgen receptor (AR) and may regulate sex-hormone signalling
Expression restricted to testis and brain; FOXG1B major transcript expressed in foetal and adult brain; four alternative multi-exon transcripts expressed in foetal brain
Critical for forebrain development; required for establishment of ventral identity in the telencephalon; postnatal expression in areas of neurogenesis may explain acquired microcephaly
RT-PCR failed to amplify FOXG1 transcripts in patient leucocytes and lymphoblastoid cells (inconclusive for mRNA stability/NMD)
Mouse (Foxg1)

Foxg1 in mouse: microcephaly with reduction in volume of neocortex and hippocampus; critical for forebrain development; participates in early telencephalon patterning at ~E8.5 in concert with Fgf signalling; required for ventral telencephalon identity; implicated in olfactory system development; brain phenotype evocative though not identical to FOXG1-related human phenotype
